column1: # Known differences against the X_ITE oracle for synthetic-externproto-reload.
# Every line is a deliberate difference (IMPLEMENTATION_SAFETY). The Rust behavior in these steps is
# asserted directly by the tests of crates/x3d-script/tests/extern_reload.rs.
# X_ITE keeps both its `construct` and `update` interests on an instance after a failed load, so the next
# successful load realizes the body of an instance twice (here: Explicit; "B initialize level=5" twice).

column5: X_ITE builds one instance's body twice after a failed load; Rust builds one body per instance
same duplicate body after a failed load

column1: # An older request that finishes after a newer one was made replaces the result for a frame in X_ITE
# (B is realized, then C). Rust drops the older result: B is never realized, C completes one frame later.

column5: older request must not replace the newer one

column1: # `load` set to FALSE while a request is in flight: X_ITE still activates the declaration when the
# request completes. Rust keeps it NOT_STARTED with its old PROTO and bodies.

column5: disabled declaration must not become active from an old request

column1: # X_ITE caches a failed fetch for good: the same URL asked for again dies with a TypeError ("Cannot read
# properties of null (reading 'setWorldURL')") although the file exists by then. Rust fetches again.

column5: a resource that becomes available must be loadable again

column1: # X_ITE lets a load of a removed declaration finish and replace the bodies; Rust cancels the load.

column5: a removed declaration keeps no active load

column1: # A Script in an instance body that is replaced or removed gets `shutdown ()` (ISO/IEC 14772-1 4.12.3,
# "invoked when the corresponding Script node is deleted"). X_ITE has no shutdown call, so its console lacks
# the "A shutdown" / "B shutdown" lines. Rust follows the standard; R0.3-D asserts it in extern_reload.rs.

column5: Script.shutdown () runs when its instance body is disposed (4.12.3); X_ITE never calls it
